name: MercadoLibre
thesis: Latin America's e-commerce + fintech compounder built on the lowest cost-to-serve. (1) Marketplace GMV (1P + 3P) compounds on category penetration and the logistics flywheel (Mercado Envios) - unit shipping costs keep falling as density builds; (2) Mercado Pago scales fintech with risk-adjusted interest income (NIMAL) as credit + payments grow ahead of GMV; (3) decades of management execution credibility. Core call: the market is too scared about credit performance while NPLs are stable and well-provisioned. Deliberate near-term margin compression (free-shipping thresholds, 1P, cross-border, credit, AI) is ACCEPTED as investment for share - it is not a thesis breaker. The real leg to watch is NIMAL (risk-adjusted spread), which compresses structurally as the lower-spread credit-card book grows.
key_driver: Logistics cost-to-serve flywheel (GMV) + Mercado Pago TPV and risk-adjusted spread (NIMAL); stable credit NPLs vs the market's fear

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <20% for 2 consecutive Qs (marketplace scale thesis stalls)

tier_1_kpis.name: MercadoPago TPV growth (FXN)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: TPV growth materially below GMV growth for 2 Qs (fintech engine slowing)

tier_1_kpis.name: Credit portfolio 90+ day NPL
tier_1_kpis.current: 17.6% Q1'26 (-40bps YoY); reserve coverage 149% of 90+ past-due
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: 90+ day NPL >21% for 2 consecutive Qs (the credit fear validated)

tier_1_kpis.name: Credit portfolio 15-90 day NPL
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Early-bucket NPL rising sharply for 2 Qs (leading indicator of 90+ deterioration)

tier_1_kpis.name: Total credit portfolio
tier_1_kpis.current: $14.6B (+87% YoY); credit card now 46% of book

tier_1_kpis.name: NIMAL (net interest margin after losses)
tier_1_kpis.current: 17.8% Q1'26 (vs 22.7% Q1'25, 23.3% Q4'25) - compressing as the lower-spread card book reached 46%, but still above the 15% floor
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: NIMAL <15% for 2 consecutive Qs (PM floor revised to 15%+; 17.8% currently clears it - card-mix compression is the expected yield-for-scale trade-off)

tier_1_kpis.name: Operating margin (consolidated) - compression accepted
tier_1_kpis.current: 6.9% Q1'26 (-600bps YoY; deliberate investment, op income -20% YoY)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Op margin <4% for 2Q or outright operating losses (real break; deliberate compression to mid-single-digits for share is accepted)

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: ROE below 20% for 2 consecutive Qs (PM floor; 31.3% currently clears it comfortably)

thesis_breakers_qualitative: 90+ day NPL above 21% for 2 consecutive Qs (credit fear validated)
Consolidated operating losses (vs accepted deliberate compression)
Logistics unit cost stops falling (the cost-to-serve moat erodes)
Latin America macro shock that breaks consumer spending

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters - outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs - cash conversion broken. (Universal floor; note MELI FCF is lumpy as the credit book grows.)
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

business_model_rules.narrative: GMV FX-neutral <20% for 2Q - marketplace scale thesis stalls (MELI ran 30-50% historically; relaxed from 25 to capture sentiment).
Mercado Pago TPV FX-neutral <25% - fintech leg loses momentum.
90+ day NPL >21% for 2Q - the market's credit fear is validated; replaces the mis-specified single-bucket NPL rule. Latest 90+ is 17.6% and improving.
NIMAL <15% for 2Q - risk-adjusted spread eroded below the PM's 15% floor (revised from a 20% watch; card-mix compression above 15% is the expected yield-for-scale trade-off).
Consolidated op margin <4% for 2Q - relaxed from 8 because deliberate margin investment for share is part of the thesis; sub-4 means investment is no longer discretionary.
ROE <20% for 2Q - the PM's return floor (revised up from ~15%); MELI runs ~30%+, so sub-20 means spread compression + credit-book capital intensity are overwhelming returns.
